To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the truncated ORFs3abc of the recombinant PBP-FIPV-DF2 virus is responsible for the low virulence and restricted tissue tropism in vivo, while the completed ORF3 region of the recombinants PBFIPV-R3i and PBFIPV-FECV-R3i are responsible for the FECV-like tissue tropism and restricted viremia, respectively.
ORF3 is a determinant of the macrophage/ monocyte tropism in vitro and the intestinal tropism in vivo.
the truncated ORFs of FCoVs are important determinants for the development of FIP and the completion of these regions can change the biotype of the viruses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of viral determinants that are important for the development of feline infectious peritoneal disease.
the identification of the genetic determinants of the FCoV biotypes and their contribution to the pathogenesis of FIP.
the identification of viral determinants responsible for the tropism of FCoVs and the development of feline infectious peritoneal diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ORF3abc has a decisive role in FIPV virulence, but is dispensable for the FECV replication in the gut.
the ORF3abc has an important role in FCoV pathogenesis, which is manifested in the tropism of the virus, the severity of disease and the serological response.
the ORF3 region is responsible for the tropism and pathogenicity of FIPV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ORF3abc region of FCoV is a determinant factor of the biotypes of the virus.
the ORF3abc region of FCoV is responsible for the tropism and virulence of FCoVs.
ORF3 plays an important role not only in the macrophage tropism but also in the pathogenicity of FIPV.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ORF3abc region plays a crucial role in the virulence and pathogenesis of FIPV, but it is also a major determinant of the biotype of the virus, which is important for the epidemiology of the disease.
a single amino acid change in a viral gene can alter its virulence in vivo.
the in vivo characteristics of FCoV are highly dependent on the ORF3 region.
